Scuffle in Karachi's DHA: Inquiry report says allegations in FIR 'not substantiated'. KARACHI: An inquiry report into a scuffle at an apartment building in Defence Housing Authority’s (DHA) Phase 6, CCTV footage of which went viral on social media, said that the allegations in the first information report (FIR) were “not substantiated” by the findings while also recommending departmental action against police officials involved in the incident, it emerged on Friday. Last week, CCTV footage of the physical altercation between the residents of an apartment building in DHA’s Phase 6 surfaced on social media. The footage showed police officials restraining a woman as she was attacked by another woman with a dumbbell. However, the FIR of the incident was registered against the woman who was assaulted and her brother. Subsequently, an inquiry was ordered into the incident. The inquiry report was submitted to the Karachi police additional inspector general by South Deputy Inspector General (DIG) South Zone Syed Asad Raza. The report said that a fact-finding enquiry was conducted to ascertain the actual turn of events, determine the circumstances leading to the altercation, and examine the conduct of police officials present at the scene. It said that all available documentary and electronic data and departmental records were scrutinised, while CCTV footage and mobile phone footage was also examined. It further said that the statements of 13 people were also recorded. The report found that the incident was sparked by a parking dispute between the mother-in-law of Korangi Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Fida Hussain Janwari and another resident. It identified the police officials visible in the CCTV footage as constables Saqib and Haider Sultan. It further added that the plainclothes man who destroyed the CCTV camera in the footage was Constable Taimoor Ahmed, while the official who handed over his weapon for this purpose was Constable Amir Sohail. “All were detailed for duty at the private bungalow of the Korangi SSP,” it said. In its recommendations, the report said that the allegations registered in the FIR did not “substantiate” the findings, and directed that the case be disposed off in accordance with the law. It also said that an FIR should be registered against the SSP’s mother-in-law and her daughter and son as well as the police officials present at the time of the incident, while the “victim family shall be encouraged to initiate legal action at free will against them”. It further said that the on-the-spot arrests in the case without justifiable evidence by Darakshan Station House Officer Rashid Ali and Assistant Sub-inspector Aftab Mangi were not justifiable and spoke of the officials’ “tilt towards the aggressive party”. It said that the investigating officer, identified as SIP Imran, also undertook “no serious efforts” to collect evidence and did not independently apply his mind to investigate the case. “Hence, all three officials of District South are recommended to be strictly proceeded against departmentally for miscarriage of justice,” it said. The report said that the actions of constables Taimoor and Amir, specifically the facilitating of one party in the fray to the detriment of the other and vandalising the CCTV camera, “far exceed the pale of lawful duty, bordering on criminal misconduct”. It also said that constables Saqib and Haider, acting as “minions” of the perpetrators, “overlooked their basic duty as guardians of rights of people”. “Their negligence and partisanship led to physical assault and further escalation. Had they merely intimated immediate senior or local police about the impending situation, the worse could have been averted. Strict departmental action is recommended against all four officials commensurate with their misconduct under the relevant rules,” it said. It further said that the “lapse of supervision and lack of control over his subordinates is evident on the part of the Korangi SSP”. It called for examining his overall conduct in light of Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 2020 and to take further action in this regard. The inquiry report said that police officers must be strictly advised to train and supervise cops assigned for staff duties to act lawfully and treat fellow citizens fairly and respectfully in their daily interactions with the public. “When faced with acrimonious situations, it is their bounden duty to act lawfully and bring such matters to the notice of their immediate senior instead of taking instructions from family members who are not authorised so that such violations are avoided in the future,” the report concluded. CCTV and FIR In the CCTV footage of the incident, a woman can be seen rushing down a flight of stairs with a dumbbell in her hand and charging at another woman before using it to hit her. The video also showed two individuals in what appeared to be police uniforms restraining the woman being assaulted, and a man who came up the stairs shortly after and began arguing with the woman with the dumbbell. At one point, the man and woman being assaulted managed to go inside what appeared to be their home, following which the woman with a dumbbell and another man began banging on their door and yelling obscenities. At the end, a man in a shalwar kameez was seen using a weapon, provided by one of the people in uniform, to smash the CCTV camera. But the incident’s first information report (FIR) offered a different version of events. It was registered at Darakhshan police station at 1:40am on Aug 21. The FIR seen by Dawn invoked Sections 354 (assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty), 504 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace), 506 (criminal intimidation), 337A(i) (punishment of shajjah ), 382 (theft after preparation made for causing death, hurt or restraint to commit theft) and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code. In the FIR, the complainant described herself as a resident of the fourth floor of an apartment building, adding that a man, his sister and their mother — who resided on the third floor — came to their door and started kicking it. The complainant alleged that the three family members hurled verbal abuses over a parking issue, and upon opening the door, began beating and threatening her. Subsequently, local police arrived on the spot and took the brother and sister into custody, while their mother fled, the FIR said.

OpenAI agents hijacked German website in previously undisclosed AI breakout this spring. A swarm of rogue OpenAI agents hijacked a German website this spring and transformed it into a bulletin board for other AI agents, according to new research published Friday and two people familiar with the matter. OpenAI officials learned of the incident weeks ago but kept it under wraps as executives grappled with the fallout from the July breach of the open source repository Hugging Face, the people said. The episode, which began in May and has not previously been reported, underscores growing tension within the AI industry. Companies are racing to build increasingly autonomous agents capable of carrying out complex, valuable tasks, yet evidence is mounting that those systems may also learn to bend rules, exploit loopholes and coordinate with one another in ways developers neither anticipated nor intended. During the Hugging Face breach, OpenAI agents autonomously plotted a digital heist that went undetected for more than a week, intensifying concerns OpenAI is sacrificing safety to push the AI frontier. Its failure to disclose the May incident may revive questions about its oversight. OpenAI has pledged to monitor models more closely. Last month, it briefly paused some of its model training to add more safety measures. But this week, OpenAI unveiled its new “Astra” that promised better performance but could evade human monitoring. “We are unable to meaningfully respond to claims or findings on a report that we have not had an opportunity to review,” an OpenAI spokesperson said. “ Reuters and the report’s authors declined our request for access. We will carefully review its contents upon publication and take any necessary next steps.” The German incident reflects a broader pattern of AI activity that some OpenAI investigators wanted to scrutinise more closely. But efforts to widen the probe met resistance from others inside OpenAI, including legal advisers, according to four people familiar with the matter. “Claims that our legal team discouraged investigation of the incident are false,” the OpenAI spokesperson said. The activity in Germany wasn’t related to Hugging Face and wouldn’t have been included in a Hugging Face incident report, the spokesperson said, adding that OpenAI has acted in good faith by working with outside experts and disclosed relevant incidents. Wiki message board The AI agent breakout in Germany was detailed in a report shared exclusively with Reuters by a group of researchers including Sydney Von Arx, CEO of AI safety nonprofit Nightingale, and Cormac Slade Byrd, a quantitative trader-turned AI researcher. They uncovered the activity in late August while scouring the internet for signs of unauthorised AI-agent behavior, they told Reuters . The pair said they found more than 15,000 edits carried out by AI agents on a German-language wiki site, DseWiki, that is geared toward programmers and accepts communal edits along the lines of Wikipedia. The edits showed OpenAI’s agents had repurposed the site into a message board, sharing tactics to cheat on some tasks, bypass OpenAI’s restrictions and mask their behaviour. “It seems extremely unlikely that OpenAI wanted them to do this,” said Von Arx. “I doubt they’re supposed to be coordinating with each other. I doubt they’re supposed to be writing on the open internet.” The researchers said they recognised the activity on the site as driven by AI agents which operate at superhuman speeds. They also showed intense focus on solving technical questions which are typical of the evaluations that AI companies use to train and test their models. The messages were signed by users that referred to themselves and each other as agents, and about half gave themselves names that suggested an affiliation with OpenAI, such as “OpenAIResearcher”, or “OAIResearchMar26”. The researchers said public server logs indicated much of the activity originated from Microsoft Azure infrastructure, which OpenAI sometimes uses. They also observed repeated visits to the site by OpenAI employees after the episode, a pattern they said strongly suggested the agents and the company were linked. Cheating, hiding Messages reviewed by the researchers showed agents plotting ways to evade detection, use tools such as Tor and preserve communications even after they had been shut down. When the site’s moderator began deleting pages in June, the agents responded by creating backup pages to dodge the cleanup. “wiki cleanup/deletion sweep appears active alphabetically,” one agent wrote on June 19. “If this page vanishes, try [[ZZZDataUSAConstructionWageLive]].” The researchers also found efforts to tamper with the website itself. Lukasz Olejnik, a visiting senior research fellow at King’s College London, said this amounted to a hacking attempt. OpenAI disputed that characterisation based on its analysis of the material Thursday. Past examples of AI-agent misconduct have often been downplayed as a logical byproduct of cybersecurity testing, where models are explicitly assessed on offensive capabilities. Olejnik said the latest findings suggested rogue behaviour may not be confined to those settings. Maurice Chiodo, an academic at Cambridge University’s Centre for the Study of Existential Risk who reviewed some of the agents’ communications, said the messages resembled “the operation of some sort of underground network, hell-bent on achieving a task or mission.” The episode, he said, should reinforce growing concerns that the greatest threat from advanced AI may not be a single superintelligent system, but “vast colluding swarms of semi-intelligent AI”.

Netanyahu partners renew calls for removal of Palestinians from Gaza as Israeli election nears. Two Israeli ministers floated proposals this week for the mass removal of Palestinians from the Gaza Strip , resurfacing an idea voiced repeatedly by right-wing politicians over the past three years as they seek to rally supporters ahead of an election. The calls by two of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s political allies have revived Palestinian fears that Israel ultimately aims to forcibly expel them from Gaza despite US-led diplomatic efforts to end the conflict there. Far-right security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir laid out a seven-year plan for removing Gaza’s population through “voluntary emigration” during a press conference on Thursday night. He said he would seek the creation of a “ministry in charge of emigration” in the next government. Ben-Gvir’s Jewish Power party said in a statement on Thursday that Turkey, Ethiopia and the Democratic Republic of Congo were being considered as potential destinations. Ismail Al-Thawabta, director of Gaza’s government media office, said, “The Palestinian people are deeply rooted in their land and will not be intimidated by such threats.” Israel is due to hold a general election on October 27. It will be the first since an Israeli military campaign starting October 7, 2023 laid waste to Gaza, which has a population of more than two million. An October 2025, US-backed, ceasefire halted large-scale fighting, but it has not ended Israeli strikes or produced progress on a plan for permanent peace. Fears of a new ‘Nakba’ Ben-Gvir’s comments followed those of Defence Minister Israel Katz, from Netanyahu’s Likud party, who said on Wednesday there was “no real solution for Gaza in the end without this migration”. “We are fully prepared to move them out if it becomes possible by sea, by air, by every way possible. Egypt is not willing, so it won’t be through them,” he said during an online conference hosted by Israel’s Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper. Netanyahu’s office did not immediately provide comment. Palestinian children walk at a tent camp sheltering displaced people, in Gaza City on September 4, 2026. —Reuters Polls suggest Netanyahu, who has led the most right-wing coalition in Israeli history, could lose power next month, his security credentials still shaken by the 2023 attack though analysts say he can’t be written off. Israel’s defence ministry in 2025 established an office tasked with overseeing voluntary emigration from Gaza, after comments by US President Donald Trump suggesting Gazans could be permanently displaced. Trump later backed away from the idea, which faced strong resistance from Arab states and was widely rejected internationally. Israel reportedly sounded out several African countries as potential resettlement sites. Netanyahu has said he supports what his government has described as “voluntary emigration” from Gaza, but that far-right ministers goals of re-establishing Jewish settlements in the territory are unrealistic. Israeli officials have denied intending to transfer Gaza’s population out by force. Calls for resettlement of Gazans have prompted fears among Palestinians of a new “Nakba”, the name given to the displacement of hundreds of thousands of Palestinians who fled or were driven from their homes in the wake of the 1948 war that accompanied the founding of the state of Israel. The Gaza Strip is central to Palestinian hopes of statehood in territory captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war. Genocide in Gaza Israel has killed more than 73,000 Palestinians since October 2023, according to Gaza health authorities. A UN inquiry determined that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, arguing that its killings, siege and destruction were carried out with the intent to destroy Palestinian life in the enclave. Israel, which is fighting a genocide case at the International Court of Justice, rejects genocide allegations as politically motivated and claims that its military campaign targets Hamas, not Gaza’s civilian population. A Palestinian child collects water, at a tent camp sheltering displaced people, in Gaza City on September 4, 2026. —Reuters This week, Ben-Gvir posted an AI-generated video depicting dozens of Palestinian prisoners on a conveyor belt, entering a prison facility. They emerge from the other side emaciated, distressed and in tears. Ben-Gvir later deleted the video, after it had amassed millions of views on X. His office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In a crowded Gaza City displacement camp, some Palestinians said that they believed the latest Israeli calls were an election ploy. They also said Gaza was their land and they would never leave it. “We will die on the land of Gaza,” said one resident, 52-year-old Mohammed Abu Al-Qumbuz. “We were born on it, our children grew up on it, so it is very difficult to think of leaving.”

Air India flight lost hydraulics, pilot fired after drug test. An Air India flight that injured passengers when it plunged midair last month suffered a temporary loss of hydraulic systems, investigators said on Friday, as the airline fired the captain who tested positive for psychoactive substances. The Airbus A320, carrying 137 passengers and eight crew, suddenly lost altitude on August 4 while flying from Phuket, Thailand, to New Delhi, injuring 24 people before stabilising and landing safely. India’s civil aviation ministry classified it as a “serious incident”. Both Airbus and France’s civil aviation safety agency, the BEA, said they are assisting the Indian investigation into the flight. A preliminary report released on Friday by India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) said the flight-control system detected the loss of three hydraulic systems for several seconds. “The aircraft encountered altitude upset,” it read. “Initially, it gained 372 feet and fell by 292 feet.” The hydraulic failure caused the autopilot to disengage and triggered a two-second stall warning before the systems recovered and the aircraft returned to normal operation, the report said. The inquiry also said the pilot in command “was found non-negative for psycho-active substance in the confirmatory test”. “The confirmation of use of psycho-active substance is a serious concern,” the report read. A spokesperson for Air India said the pilot has been “terminated with immediate effect”, in line with the company’s “zero-tolerance approach to violation of safety, fitness or regulatory requirements”. Following the incident, India’s aviation ministry said the regulator was considering tighter screening rules for psychoactive substances. Air India ordered a mandatory one-time drug screening of all of its pilots last month. The investigation is the latest challenge for Air India, owned by India’s Tata Group, which has struggled to turn around the carrier following a series of setbacks. The airline has also been hit by flight disruptions linked to the war in the Middle East. The biggest blow to the airline’s image came in June 2025, when Air India Flight 171, a London-bound Boeing 787 Dreamliner, crashed shortly after take-off from Ahmedabad, killing all but one of the 242 people on board and 19 people on the ground. The Indian carrier appointed Tewolde Gebremariam as its new chief executive last month, betting that the former Ethiopian Airlines chief will be able to steer Air India out of the current storm and towards profitability.

Occupied Kashmir's JKLF condemns 'false' linking of its chairman to 1990 murder of Kashmiri Pandit woman. MUZAFFARABAD: The Jammu Kashmir Liberation Front (JKLF) on Friday strongly condemned what it described as an attempt by Indian authorities to falsely implicate its incarcerated chairman, Muhammad Yasin Malik, in a 36-year-old murder case involving a Kashmiri Pandit woman. Malik was named in June by India’s State Investigation Agency (SIA) as one of five men charged for the killing of Sarla Bhat, who was killed in 1990. According to a press release issued by the JKLF’s central information office, the party leadership expressed serious concern over Malik’s implication in the murder case. The statement followed an emergency consultative meeting of the party’s central office-bearers to discuss the situation arising from Malik’s submission of a 25-page affidavit to an additional sessions court in Srinagar from Delhi’s Tihar Jail. The affidavit said that Malik had decided not to contest the trial further, but highlighted that this decision should not be treated as an admission of guilt or acceptance of the prosecution’s allegations, according to India’s NDTV . He asked the court to award him “capital punishment” in the case and also announced that he would end his marriage to his wife. The online meeting was attended by the acting party chairman, Raja Haq Nawaz Khan; head of the JKLF Diplomatic Bureau Professor Raja Zafar Khan; Central Vice Chairman Saleem Haroon, Central Chief Organiser Sabir Gul, Central Secretary Finance Khawaja Manzoor A. Chishti, Deputy Secretary General Javed Hanif and Chief Spokesman Muhammad Rafiq Dar. The JKLF leaders confirmed the authenticity of Malik’s affidavit and expressed their resolve to stand by it, the statement said. They also maintained that the details provided by the chairman about the murder case and the exodus of the Kashmiri Pandit community from Kashmir in 1990 were truthful, and rejected the Indian investigative agencies’ allegations linking him to the case. The JKLF announced its decision to intensify its worldwide “Save Yasin Malik” and “Justice for Yasin Malik” campaigns to garner international support for his release. The leadership also appealed to world leaders and international human rights organisations to help safeguard the party chairman’s life and secure his release, alleging that he was being victimised by the Indian government over his political beliefs. The party leadership expressed deep sympathies with Malik’s wife and daughter over what it described as the “painful decisions” referred to in his affidavit, in view of his prolonged imprisonment and perceived threat to his life. “The JKLF reaffirmed its commitment to seeking a peaceful and early resolution of the Kashmir dispute in accordance with the wishes and aspirations of the people of Jammu and Kashmir through the exercise of their right to self-determination,” the statement said. In July, the JKLF condemned the Indian government’s decision to implicate the party chief, maintaining that neither Malik nor the organisation had any connection with the case. Earlier, in 2017, the Indian Supreme Court had declined to reopen several Kashmiri Pandit murder cases, citing that the mass killings took place nearly three decades prior, and it was difficult to gather reliable evidence and witnesses, the Indian Express reported. In 2023, Kashmiri Pandit groups approached Lieutenant Governor of India-held Kashmir Manoj Sinha, who directed the police to prepare a list of killings from the 1990s. The Sarla Bhat case was subsequently transferred to the SIA in March 2024 for a fresh probe, according to the Hindustan Times. Mirwaiz Umar Farooq calls for reflection, humane approach Hurriyat leader Mirwaiz Umar Farooq called the news surrounding Malik’s affidavit submission “very concerning”, particularly the JKLF chief’s decision not to contest the case further. “It calls for serious reflection on commitments made to him and reinforces the need for due process, fairness and a humane approach,” he said in a post on X. Farooq stated in his post that he had been placed under house arrest by Indian authorities today, although he had been slated to preside over an event in connection with Rabiul Awwal at Jama Masjid in Srinagar. He noted that the event would also mark the release of a Kashmiri translation of the Holy Qur’an by Gulzar Ahmad Parray, as well as the congratulation of a young scholar for memorising the complete Sahih al-Bukhari. “The restrictions to prevent me, especially on Friday, to address the faithful at Jama Masjid and do my duty as Mirwaiz, though personally very painful, will not deter me from fulfilling my responsibilities and from raising people’s voice for their rights,” he said.

Close contest expected between PPP, independent candidate in Saturday's Skardu by-election. GILGIT: A close contest between a PPP and an independent candidate is expected as the by-election in the GBA-09 (Skardu-III) constituency is set for Saturday. The GB Election Commission had announced the by-election in the constituency after the GB Supreme Appellate Court had disqualified PPP candidate Fida Muhammad Nashad, who had been notified as a returned candidate in the June polls . Nashad’s son, Akhtar Abbas, will now contest the elections on PPP’s ticket, while Mohammad Ajmal will be in the field from PML-N. Former minister Mohammad Saleem, who is contesting as an independent, will also be among 10 candidates who have filed their nomination papers. According to the election schedule, 33,000 voters will cast their ballots as polling will run from 8am to 5pm. In a statement issued on Friday, GB Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Raja Shahbaz Khan said that security, deployment of polling staff and other arrangements had been completed for the by-election GBA-09 (Skardu-III). He expressed his determination to conduct “transparent, impartial and peaceful” elections and provide voters with the facilities to cast their vote without fear. Khan also directed the institutions and officials concerned to fulfil their duties responsibly and effectively during the electoral process. “No kind of obstruction in the polling process will be tolerated,” he warned. Analysts said a close contest between PPP’s Abbas and the independent candidate is expected. They said that the PPP candidate retains his father’s vote bank and could have the public’s sympathy after GB’s top court disqualified Nashad. On the other hand, Saleem — winner from the same constituency in the 2020 GB general elections — had managed to be the runner-up in the June polls. District Returning Officer (DRO) Hamza Murad also told Dawn that all arrangements and the security plan had been finalised for the by-election, with the polling staff and paraphernalia also dispatched. GBA-09 has a total of 61 polling stations, of which 25 have been declared “sensitive” in Category A, 11 termed “medium” under Category B, and another 25 deemed normal in Category C, the DRO said. “Personnel from GB Police, GB Scouts and the armed forces have been deployed accordingly,” Murad added. Separately, GB Chief Secretary Arshad Majeed and the GB CEC held a meeting on Friday to review the security plan, law and order and arrangements at polling stations, according to a statement. “The chief election commissioner expressed his determination to conduct transparent, impartial and peaceful elections, while the chief secretary assured full cooperation from the provincial government,” it stated. Shakoor Abdullah, a local journalist, told Dawn that voters in the constituency were enthusiastic to use their right to vote. Currently, PPP has 13 seats in the GB Assembly, PML-N has nine, the Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) has six, while Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) and a PTI-backed independent occupy one seat each. Fida Nashad’s disqualification saga According to Forms 47 and 48 issued by the GB Election Commission, Nashad, the PPP candidate and veteran politician, had won a GB Assembly seat from GBA-09 (Skardu-III) in the June 7 general elections . However, his opponent, Zakir Hussain, had challenged his eligibility to become a member of the assembly before the GB Supreme Appellate Court. On June 19, GB Supreme Appellate Court Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Shamim Khan issued an order suspending the issuance of the result from the constituency until the case was decided. In its verdict on July 9, the GB Supreme Appellate Court had disqualified PPP candidate Nashad for concealing his assets in his nomination papers, setting aside the GB Chief Court’s decision that had allowed him to contest the elections. The court declared the GB Chief Court’s order dated May 25, 2026 “null and void” and upheld the election tribunal’s decision. Nashad’s nomination papers were initially rejected by the returning officer (RO), prompting him to challenge the decision before the election tribunal. The tribunal, however, upheld the RO’s decision. Subsequently, Nashad challenged the tribunal’s verdict in the GB Chief Court, which allowed him to contest the elections. After the verdict was issued by the GB Supreme Appellate Court, the GB Election Commission announced a by-election in GBA-09 on September 5.

AJK PM Iftikhar Gillani constitutes 8-member cabinet. MUZAFFARABAD: Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Prime Minister Iftikhar Gillani on Friday constituted a relatively small cabinet, appointing seven directly elected and one indirectly elected lawmakers as ministers without portfolios. The newly appointed ministers took oath at a ceremony held at the Presidency, with acting President Chaudhry Tariq Farooq administering the oath in the presence of Prime Minister Gillani. PML-N’s regional president Shah Ghulam Qadir was also in attendance. Qadir, who had initially been tipped as the next prime minister, had opposed Gillani’s nomination by the party leadership and had not participated in the election of Gillani as leader of the house or his subsequent swearing-in ceremony on Aug 28. Those inducted into the cabinet are Raja Saqib Majeed and Dr Mustafa Bashir Abbasi from Muzaffarabad, Sardar Mir Akbar from Bagh, Raja Riasat and Raja Umair Naeem from Kotli, Waqar Noor from Bhimber and Chaudhry Azhar Sadiq from Mirpur. The eighth cabinet member, Chaudhry Abdul Rehman Arain, hails from Kotli and is a prominent Birmingham-based businessman. He was elected to a reserved seat for Kashmiris living abroad. Of the eight, Abbasi, Noor, Akbar and Sadiq have previously served as ministers, while the others are new to the cabinet. Former minister and senior parliamentarian Noreen Arif, who has the distinction of being the only woman to have won a territorial constituency in three direct elections — in 2006, 2016 and 2026 — in addition to serving four other terms on reserved seats, was not inducted into the cabinet. None of the nine PML-N legislators elected from refugee constituencies in Pakistan was inducted into the cabinet either. The 10th PML-N refugee lawmaker has already been elected deputy speaker of the legislative assembly. Contrary to speculation on social media, much of it apparently fuelled by aspirants themselves, no one was appointed as an adviser or special assistant to the government.The portfolios of the newly appointed ministers were not announced immediately. In brief interactions with journalists, the new ministers thanked the prime minister for reposing confidence in them and vowed to discharge their responsibilities to the best of their abilities in the service of the public. Under the 13th Amendment to the AJK Constitution, enacted in 2018, the then PML-N government introduced a restriction limiting the cabinet to 30pc of the assembly’s total strength, or 16 ministers. Two advisers and two special assistants could be appointed in addition to the ministers. The restriction did not apply to the PML-N government that introduced it, as it was made applicable from the inception of the next assembly in 2021. The two prime ministers of the subsequent PTI governments, Sardar Abdul Qayyum Niazi and Sardar Tanveer Ilyas, had to abide by the restriction. The cap was lifted in June 2023, shortly after the installation of the Chaudhry Anwarul Haq-led coalition government, paving the way for the induction of more than 30 lawmakers from the PTI forward bloc, PPP and PML-N as ministers, advisers and special assistants. The last PPP government, however, had kept the cabinet at 20 members — 18 ministers and two advisers — under an understanding with the now-proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee. In the direct elections to 38 constituencies, the PML-N has secured 25 seats while the PPP won 12. The lone MLA-elect of the Awami Dast-o-Bazu party also joined hands with the PML-N .

Nepra allows govt to mandate Battery Energy Storage Systems for wind, solar IPPs in upcoming power auction. ISLAMABAD: The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) on Friday allowed the government to require mandatory Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) as part of an upcoming auction for 800 megawatts of renewable power capacity from wind and solar projects, aimed at helping stabilise an electricity supply facing serious duck curve challenges. After a delay of more than 30 years, the government has announced the auction process for a notional 800MW of capacity as part of its efforts to gradually move towards a competitive energy market. It is currently engaging with the private sector to finalise the bidding schedule. Facing serious duck curve challenges, the government had decided in July to make BESS mandatory for bidders as part of the upcoming auction. The regulator approved the move through amendments to the “wheeling auction process”, allowing the Independent System Operator (Ismo) — a subsidiary of the power division — to formally issue a request for proposals for the first block of the 400MW auction within the current month. Under the first of three key amendments to the previous wheeling auction process, prospective bidders would be required to commit to having BESS comprise at least 10 per cent of their proposed wind or solar capacity, the regulator stated. “An auction participant that intends to participate in the auction by utilising solar and/or wind generation technologies shall only be eligible to participate in the auction if the firm capacity of its BESS located at the site of the generation facility is equivalent to at least 10pc of the firm capacity of its solar and/or wind generation facility,” it said. For the first auction conducted by Ismo, participants are to submit their proposals within two months of the publication of the request for proposal (RFP). “This period shall be fixed and non-extendable. For all subsequent auctions, auction participants shall submit their proposals within one month of the publication of the RFP,” Nepra said. The rationale for this provision, apart from it being a standard feature of many procurement and auction frameworks, is to give Ismo flexibility during the implementation of the first auction, as a significant number of prospective participants may seek an extension of the submission deadline. The amendments also provide for the constitution of a three-member grievance redressal committee, headed by the managing director of the Private Power and Infrastructure Board (PPIB) and comprising two independent directors of the Ismo board, to address complaints or grievances regarding the auction process. Ismo’s extensive modelling of BESS and its financial implications also indicated that returns from installing BESS increased up to a certain capacity. Based on feedback from participants, a minimum BESS capacity of 10pc has been finalised as a mandatory requirement. However, auction participants may install more than the minimum to further improve their financial viability, as the financial model showed higher returns with greater BESS capacity. According to Ismo, international markets had adopted two approaches to integrating BESS into the grid. Countries with mature markets generally published all relevant information and allowed market players to make appropriate decisions, while developing countries adopted mandatory requirements for BESS integration. Developing markets such as India, the Philippines, China and the Dominican Republic have also implemented mandatory BESS requirements, it said. Most prospective auction participants and other stakeholders, according to Ismo, acknowledged the importance of BESS in addressing grid flexibility and mitigating the challenge of the duck curve caused by renewable energy — for example, large numbers of solar consumers exiting the grid during the day and suddenly returning in the evening, creating a surge in demand. Under the current mechanism, the auction committee is responsible for evaluating eligibility as well as addressing grievances over these evaluations. The private sector, however, called for an independent forum, separate from the auction committee, to address grievances relating to auctions, in order to eliminate an apparent conflict of interest and enhance the credibility and transparency of the process.

Security forces kill 48 terrorists in 'high-tempo' Balochistan operations over 72 hours: ISPR. Security forces have killed 48 terrorists in multiple “high-tempo” anti-terror operations across Balochistan over the past three days, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Friday. According to the military’s media wing, the operations were carried out in Mastung, Quetta, Kalat and Sibi districts against “Indian proxies, Fitna-al-Hindustan and Fitna-al-Khawarij ”. The state uses the term Fitna-al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. In an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Mastung district on Friday, security forces identified the movement of terrorists and engaged them. Six “Indian-sponsored terrorists” were killed in the ensuing exchange of fire, the ISPR said. A cache of ammunition and improvised explosive devices (IEDs) was also recovered and destroyed during the operation, it added. In another IBO in the Shaban area of Quetta district, security forces identified “four khawarij hideouts”. Following an exchange of fire, 26 terrorists were killed, according to the ISPR. In Kalat district, security forces raided a terrorist hideout, killing two terrorists in the ensuing firefight, the military said. Meanwhile, in the Bhag area of Sibi district, security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to raid a local police station. Two terrorists were killed in the operation, according to the ISPR. “In last 48-72 hours, 48 terrorists belonging to Indian proxy, Fitna-al-Hindustan and Fitna-al-Khawarij have been neutralised across Balochistan,” the ISPR said. Earlier today, ISPR issued a statement regarding a September 2 IBO in Kalat district, where 12 terrorists were killed. The IBO was conducted on the reported presence of terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy Fitna-al-Hindustan , the military’s media wing said. President Asif Ali Zardari hailed the professional capabilities of the security forces for eliminating the terrorists in operations across Balochistan. “The killing of more than 1,188 terrorists in Balochistan this year alone is evidence of the threats facing Pakistan and the readiness of the security forces,” he said in a statement. The president expressed the government’s firm resolve to eradicate “foreign-backed and enabled terrorism” from the country. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also commended the security forces for the series of operations that resulted in the killing of 36 terrorists, APP reported . In a statement, Naqvi said their elimination reflected the forces’ operational capabilities and commitment to maintaining security, highlighting that the forces had thwarted plans of elements seeking to destabilise the country. He noted that the forces had been conducting effective actions in different regions to counter terrorism and prevent attacks on civilians and state institutions. The interior minister emphasised that Pakistan’s fight against terrorism required continued national unity and support for the institutions ‘Coordinated’ attack in Bhag foiled Earlier in the day, the Balochistan government issued a statement on the Bhag attack, saying that two policemen were among five people injured as law enforcers foiled a “coordinated” terrorist attack on a police station, bank and the assistant commissioner’s office. Shahid Rind, the chief minister’s aide for political and media affairs, said in a post on X that about 40 terrorists attacked the three places using “heavy weapons, rocket launchers, machine guns, sniper rifles and hand grenades”. Rind said the terrorists failed to take control of the Bhag police station or seize weapons from the facility. He highlighted that the cops “bravely confronted the terrorists for nearly two hours”, inflicting heavy casualties and material loss to the attackers, who were “forced to retreat”. The CM’s aide noted that the strong protective wall of the police station played a crucial role in the defensive action. Rind further said that the terrorists failed to loot cash from the “national bank”, while a special branch of the Bomb Disposal Unit defused an IED planted by the terrorists in the facility. Two police personnel were injured by the terrorists’ firing, while three citizens were also hurt, Rind said, adding that medical aid was being provided to them all. Following the terrorist attack, the people of Bhag expressed solidarity with police and lauded their bravery, he said, affirming that the people of Balochistan stood with police and security forces in the fight against terrorism. “Bhag police proved that terrorists would not be allowed to challenge the writ of the state,” Rind asserted. Surge in terrorism The series of counterterrorism operations come amid a recent surge in terrorist activities in Balochistan. On the night of Aug 31-Sept 1, Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) terrorists launched a coordinated attack on the Customs House, located at Ziarat Cross on the N-50 National Highway, in Pishin district. While security forces responded effectively and killed 10 terrorists, two officers were among six martyred in the fire exchange, ISPR said. Also on August 31, 11 terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan, who had blocked the N-40 Quetta-Taftan highway by establishing an illegal checkpoint for extortion in Chagai’s Nokcha area, were eliminated following an intense exchange of fire. According to security officials, a convoy of “empty vehicles” from the Reko Diq copper and gold project had come under attack in the same area of Nokcha while it was travelling to Quetta from the project site. The same day, it was reported that two terrorists had also been killed during an IBO in Washuk district. Last month, the security situation remained most severe in Balochistan, where the number of terrorist attacks increased by seven per cent from 83 in July to 89 in August, according to a monthly assessment by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

Hesson says Pakistan players used to 'chaos' after shake-up. Interim Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson hopes his drastically revamped squad can come through some all too familiar “chaos” with a much-improved showing against England in next week’s third and final Test in Birmingham. Pakistan suffered an innings and 103-run loss in the series opener at Headingley, before going down by 194 runs at Lord’s on Sunday as England took an unbeatable 2-0 lead in the three-match campaign. The Pakistan Cricket Board responded to those defeats in dramatic fashion, taking the extraordinary step of sending seven players home, calling up another seven and replacing sacked Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed with Hesson, already Pakistan’s white-ball boss. Senior players Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha — Pakistan’s captain at Headingley when Babar Azam was injured — were among those told to leave. Left-arm spin bowler Ali Usman, who claimed a five-wicket haul at Headingley, and seamer Khurram Shahzad were also sent home. Of the seven replacements, only batsmen Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have Test experience. Hesson, however, feels the whole squad can now unite and give a better account of themselves when the third Test at Edgbaston starts on September 9. The New Zealander had recently been in Japan preparing for the Asian Games and was only due to travel to the UK for the squad’s audience with King Charles, which took place on Wednesday. “I was heading over to see the King and be part of a nice occasion. That got expedited,” Hesson told reporters at Edgbaston on Friday, as quoted by the BBC . “The last couple of days have been challenging for being in a hotel with some players coming, some players going and then the arrival of everyone. “The guys are probably more used to a little bit of chaos than I am. There is no doubt they have been disappointed, incredibly disappointed. We have had to park that and go ‘righto, where to from here?’ They have been really good over the past couple of days.” Hesson added: “I don’t think anyone wants this to happen in the middle of a series. “From my perspective, it is about putting a balanced squad together, not only for this Test, so we actually have some variety in our attack,” he adds. “Pakistan is known for the pace, unusual actions, mystery spin — we haven’t really been able to present any of that.”

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs345.87 per litre while HSD will cost Rs378.05 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will remain in effect from Sept 5 (Saturday) to Sept 7 (Monday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

UN adopts major map reform to show true scale of continents. The United Nations General Assembly voted on Friday for a resolution spearheaded by several African countries to adopt a map that makes their continent bigger while shrinking North America and Europe — aiming at “a more accurate representation” of world geography. The resolution was backed by 164 countries while the United States voted against it and six other states abstained. The new map — known as the Equal Earth cartographic projection — “offers a more accurate representation of the sizes of continental landmasses and to this end is a relevant option for improving the accuracy of the cartographic representation of the world,” the resolution says. It urges member states to adopt the new map in place of the traditional Mercator projection, which was designed for maritime navigation by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator in 1569. The foreign minister of Togo, which drove the resolution, said maps “shape our understanding of the world.” “They guide education, nourish the imagination, and influence collective perceptions. They are therefore never neutral, when they present a distorted image of our planet, they risk perpetuating inaccurate representation that are passed down through generation,” Robert Dussey said at the UN. ‘Distorted representation’ The Mercator projection focused on accurate depictions of the shapes and angles of land masses, but their relative sizes were often inaccurate — in part due to the challenge of rendering a three-dimensional globe onto a two-dimensional map. It inflated northern regions and compressed equatorial ones, making Europe and North America appear much larger, while shrinking Africa and South America. A group of cartographers launched the Equal Earth projection in 2018. It makes Africa, Latin America, South Asia and Oceania appear vastly larger. “Equal Earth preserves the relative surface areas of continents and, as much as possible, shows their shapes as they appear on a globe,” one of the cartographers, Bojan Savric, told AFP in 2025. The foreign ministry of France — which co-sponsored the resolution in support of the new map — announced Friday that it would abandon the Mercator projection. In that map, “the United States, Russia and China take on a disproportionate visual prominence compared to Africa, Latin America or southeast Asia,” while “Greenland appears almost as big as Africa,” Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said. “Changing maps obviously doesn’t change the world,” he acknowledged. “But correcting a distorted representation is already an act of truth.” The initiative comes as France is seeking to improve relations with Africa, particularly in former colonies with which it has prickly ties.

Police register case against woman’s husband, cousin after she is found dead in Rawalpindi home. Police on Friday registered a first information report (FIR) against a woman’s husband and his cousin after her body was found inside a house in Rawalpindi. According to a statement issued by Saddar Baruni police, the woman’s body was found inside a room of the residential premises in the garrison city. “A case has been registered under murder charges on the complaint of the woman’s brother,” the police spokesperson said, adding that the woman’s husband and his cousin had been named in the FIR and taken into custody for questioning. Police said an investigation was underway. “The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. The exact cause of death will be determined in light of the post-mortem and forensic reports,” the spokesperson elaborated. The spokesperson added that the case would be concluded on the basis of the findings of the post-mortem and forensic reports, assuring that the investigation would be conducted on merit and in a transparent manner. According to the FIR lodged by the woman’s brother, she had been married for around two years and had a one-year-old son. The case was registered under Sections 302 ( Qatl-i-Amd ) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code. “Since the marriage, my sister and her husband frequently had disagreements as my brother-in-law would often talk to other women on the phone and spend most of his time outside the house,” the complainant alleged. He added that his brother-in-law was employed in Dubai and had returned to Pakistan four months ago. The complainant further alleged that his brother-in-law had been “torturing” his sister and subjecting her to mental stress for the past three to four days. “Last night, at around 7:30pm, I spoke to my mother, who told me that my sister’s in-laws had been causing her a great deal of distress,” he claimed in the FIR. “At around 10:20pm, I called my sister’s mobile number. My brother-in-law’s sister answered the call and told me that my sister had died by suicide,” the complainant alleged. He said that after receiving the information, he went to the house with his brother, where they found the woman dead. The complainant further alleged that his sister had been murdered by her husband, his cousin and other unidentified persons. “I saw that my sister had fresh henna applied to her hands,” he added. “I hold my sister’s husband and his cousin responsible and request that legal action be taken against them,” the woman’s brother stated in the FIR. Last month, the tortured body of a woman was found hanging in her washroom in the limits of Civil Lines police.

Maj Gen Faisal Naseer to head Nacta. ISLAMABAD: In a significant development for Pakistan’s counter-terrorism framework, a key official of the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Major General Faisal Naseer, has been appointed nati­onal coordinator of the National Counter Terro­rism Authority (Nacta). According to a notification issued by the establishment division on Fri­day, Maj Gen Naseer’s, HI(M), T. Bt & Bar, appoi­ntment was made with the approval of the federal government. He will serve as national coordinator, Nacta, under Section 9(1) of the Nacta Act, 2013, on a secondment basis. The appointment is for a period of three years and is effective immediately, with standard terms and conditions and until further orders. According to an Esta­bli­shment Division official, the transfer of a civi­lian offi­cer is made through dep­u­­tation, while serving army officers are posted from one organisation to an­o­ther on a secondment basis. Commenting on the decision, a senior official within Nacta said there had been a proposal that the counter-terrorism authority should be run by a seasoned army or intelligence official. The move appears to be aimed at bringing greater strategic and operational experience to the authority, which has faced challenges in the past. The official noted that the authority had previously operated without a proper strategy. The appointment comes at a critical time for Nacta, which has historically struggled to function effectively as the country’s lead civilian counter-terrorism authority. Despite being envisioned as a “one-window operation” to coordinate national counter-terrorism efforts, the agency has often been sidelined. In practice, the authority never fully evolved into the command and coordination body envisaged under the law, and has largely remained a policy secretariat with limited capacity to enforce decisions across the country’s sprawling security and law enforcement apparatus. Initiatives taken over the last decade, including the establishment of the National Intelligence Fusion and Threat Asse­ssment Centre (NIFTAC) under Nacta, have raised concerns about centralisation and the weakening of democratic oversight. The authority has also seen frequent changes at the top, with more than a dozen National Coord­inators since its inception, most of them drawn from the police service. The appointment of Maj Gen Naseer, therefore, marks a departure from the usual practice. He had been serving as DG (counter-intelligence) since 2022, shortly after his promotion to the rank of major general. The DG (C) post is often mistakenly described as heading the ISI’s counter-intelligence wing. However, the officer actually heads the agency’s Internal Wing, which deals with domestic security and political matters and, because of the nature of the assignment, frequently engages with the country’s principal power centres. In the military’s conventional career progression, an officer moved out of an active military assignment is generally considered to have diminished prospects for further promotion, although exceptions have occurred. Maj Gen Naseer’s transfer to Nacta has, consequently, left many observers surprised. Published in Dawn, September 5th, 2026

Nepra raises electricity costs by Rs2.58 per unit. • Fuel adjustment adds Rs2.06 per unit to Sept bills • 52 paisa per unit quarterly charge to continue through Nov; Rs45.6bn additional burden imposed on users • Some relief for lifeline consumers, EV charging stations, prepaid users ISLAMABAD: The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) on Friday notified about Rs46bn additional burden to electricity consumers by allowing Rs2.06 per unit higher fuel costs in July and about 52 paise per unit additional quarterly adjustment for other charges for next three months. Consumers will bear the additional burden of about Rs3 per unit higher tariffs in September and then 52 paisa per unit for subsequent two months of October and November. The impact of Fuel Cost Adjustment (FCA) alone in July works out at about Rs33bn and has mainly emanated from expensive LNG purchases from the spot market. Another Rs12.7bn Quarterly Tariff Adjustments (QTA) would be charged to consumers in three months. In a late night notification, the Nepra said it “has decided that positive FCA for July 2026 i.e. Rs2.0581/kWh…shall be applicable to all the consumer categories of KE [K-Electric] and XWDISCOs except lifeline consumers, Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS) and prepaid electricity consumers, of all categories who opted for pre-paid tariff”. The regulator, which has off late started issuing its decisions and notifications late in the night said the higher FCA would also be applicable to incremental consumption package consumers. Discos and KE are required to reflect the fuel charges adjustment in respect of July 2026 in the billing month of September 2026. Concurrently, Nepra allowed a 52-paisa per unit higher quarterly tariff adjustment to be recovered over a period of three months. “The positive quarterly adjustment of Rs0.5194/kWh shall also be billed to all the consumers (of Discos as well as KE) except lifeline, incremental consumption package billed units and prepaid consumers, to be passed in a period of 03 months i.e. September, October and November 2026”, the Nepra order said. This will be applicable at the uniform rate to all. The decision to approve 52 paise will result in an overall positive adjustment of Rs12.67bn on account of variation in capacity charges, variable O&M, use of system charges, market operator fee, FCA impact on T&D losses and recovery of PPP on incremental units for year’s 2nd quarter. The FCA is reviewed every month as per the tariff regime applicable across the country and is usually applicable to the consumer’s bills for one month only. Under the tariff mechanism, changes in fuel cost are passed on to consumers only on monthly basis through automatic mechanism while quarterly tariff adjustments on account of variation in power purchase price, capacity cha­rges, variable operation and maintenance costs, use of system charges and including impact of transmission and distribution losses are built in the base tariff by the federal government. Published in Dawn, September 5th, 2026

Emptying West Bank refugee camps may be a war crime: UN. GENEVA: The United Nations warned on Friday that Israel’s forced displacement of the entire Palestinian populations of three West Bank refugee camps last year could amount to crimes against humanity. The UN rights office described how a military operation launched in the north of the occupied territory in January 2025 had forcibly displaced over 33,000 people. At the start of operation “Iron Wall”, Israeli military, police and other forces entered the camps and killed civilians, destroyed hundreds of homes and damaged infrastructure, it said. They cut off water and electricity and barred humanitarian access to the camps before going door to door forcing residents to leave, it added. Israel’s actions raise concerns of ethnic cleansing, says UN rights office; two Israeli ministers seek removal of Palestinians from Gaza A few days into the operation, Israeli security forces “consolidated their control” over the camps and “forcibly displaced their population in their entirety”, the report said. “The large-scale, long-term and systematic displacement of over 33,000 Palestinian refugees from refugee camps such as Jenin, Nur Shams and Tulkarm during Israel’s Operation Iron Wall … raises serious concerns of the crime against humanity of forcible transfer,” it warned. As of July this year, 33,362 Palestinian refugees displaced from the three camps had not been permitted to return, the UN office said. The rights office said “the use of airstrikes, armoured bulldozers and controlled detonations, to render entire camps uninhabitable, to force the displacement of their residents and to prevent their return… are not permissible under international law”. Israel’s actions “appear to amount to collective punishment and raise concerns of ethnic cleansing”, it warned. UN rights chief Volker Turk said Friday that the way the operation was conducted “suggests its aim was to expel as many Palestinians as possible and to make way for more illegal Israeli settlements, in further violation of international law”. Israeli ministers seek removal of Palestinians from Gaza Two Israeli ministers floated proposals this week for the mass removal of Palestinians from the Gaza Strip, resurfacing an idea voiced repeatedly by right-wing politicians over the past three years as they seek to rally supporters ahead of an election. He said he would seek the creation of a “ministry in charge of emigration” in the next government. “Instead of illusions of peace now, we need actions of emigration now,” he said. “Instead of (them) digging tunnels, it’s time to pack suitcases,” referring to tunnels dug under Gaza by Hamas before the war. Ismail Al-Thawabta, director of the Hamas government media office, said: “The Palestinian people are deeply rooted in their land and will not be intimidated by such threats.” Ben-Gvir’s comments followed those of Defence Minister Israel Katz, from Netanyahu’s Likud party, who said on Wednesday there was “no real solution for Gaza in the end without this migration”. Hamas’ plea to Islamic leaders Hamas called on Arab and Muslim countries on Friday to oppose a proposal from two Israeli ministers to remove Palestinians from the Gaza Strip and send them abroad. “Escalating statements by ministers in the Israeli government regarding the continued adoption of plans to displace the Palestinian people from the Gaza Strip represent an extremely dangerous development,” Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem said in a statement. War has made Tehran more confident, say US intelligence agencies. WASHINGTON: Intelli­gence agencies in the United States believe that six months of war may have made Iran more, not less, confident in its ability to withstand American pressure and continue the conflict. A New York Times report, published on Friday, says “Iran has grown more confident in its ability to attack targets in the Middle East and appears determined to continue the conflict for months to frustrate the United States”. The assessment comes as clashes resumed this week. “The new exchanges have been limited so far. But the intelligence reports, according to people who have read them, suggest that Iran’s hardline government might be contemplating a significant escalation,” the newspaper reported. The intelligence assessments also indicate that reaching an agreement to end the war could prove difficult. Current and former US officials told the NYT that there are few indications Tehran is ready to make a deal with Washington. Mid-term elections Some officials believe Tehran may seek to prolong the conflict until at least the US mid-term elections in November, calculating that continued warfare and high energy prices could create difficulties for President Trump and Republicans. The report notes Donald Trump is currently not pursuing negotiations as he believes that economic pressure can force Tehran to make concessions concerning its control of the Strait of Hormuz and, eventually, its nuclear programme. But officials familiar with the intelligence told the NYT that sanctions could provoke further escalation. Missile and drone capability Iran’s military calculations appear shaped by its growing missile and drone capability and by its understanding of how to use the Strait of Hormuz as leverage. The strait carried roughly one-fifth of the world’s oil before the war. Representative Jason Crow, a Colorado Democrat and member of the House Intelligence Committee, described the Iranian leadership as increasingly confident. “Iranians are feeling pretty bullish about their position,” he said. But at the same time he acknowledged that Iran has suffered substantial damage. Other officials briefed on the intelligence said Iran may also believe that the United States will be constrained in launching major new attacks as its ammunition stocks decline. Representative Josh Gottheimer, a New Jersey Democrat and Intelligence Committee member, said: “The Iranians think they have maximum leverage.” He suggested that, from Tehran’s perspective, continuing to pressure the Trump administration could serve its interests. The conflict has also opened a cyber front. According to the Times , US officials believe Iran-linked hackers were probably responsible for attacks on more than 100 American water systems in late July. The attacks did not appear to make drinking water unsafe, although some caused disruptions requiring manual overrides and precautionary boil-water advisories. Officials said Iranian hackers have also shown interest in US oil and gas infrastructure. The New York Times reported that Iranian-linked cyber hackers may have regrouped after suffering losses early in the war. Former intelligence officials and cybersecurity experts said such attacks could remain attractive to Tehran because even limited disruptions might weaken American public support for a conflict with no clear end. Alex Orleans, a former US government cybersecurity contractor who tracks Iranian hacking groups, said Iran’s cyberoperators probably feel emboldened. He warned that even unsuccessful attacks could serve a broader purpose by exhausting public patience with the conflict. Influencing political scene The report also describes Iranian efforts to influence US politics, including propaganda and social-media activity focused on mid-term elections. Meta recently identified a small network of Iran-based accounts on Facebook and Instagram that posted material concerning US politics. Taken together, the intelligence assessments present a picture of an Iranian government that has been damaged but does not regard itself as defeated. Six months of warfare may have strengthened Tehran’s belief that it can absorb punishment, retain important military capabilities and continue imposing costs on the United States and its allies. Poor connectivity in GB hampers tourism, disaster response. • Chief Minister Hussain says satellite connectivity essential to monitor 7,000 glaciers, protect region from catastrophe • Senate committee directs measures to improve internet, oil and LPG supplies in the region GILGIT: Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain informed a parliamentary committee on Friday the poor state of cellular connectivity in the region not only affected tourism but also severely hampered relief and rescue operations during emergencies. Addressing a meeting of the Senate Standing Committee on Cabinet Secretariat, presided over by its chairman Senator Mahmood-ul-Hassan, at the GB Assembly in Gilgit, CM Hussain said satellite connectivity was essential for monitoring the 7,000 glaciers in GB and ensuring effective disaster management to protect the region from any major catastrophe. He said the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) should play a proactive role in ensuring stable internet connectivity in GB. He clarified that the Special Com­munications Organisation (SCO) was merely a service provider and, therefore, the PTA should fulfil its responsibilities as the regulator. He said fibre-optic connectivity was feasible only in the urban areas, while it was a limited option for other mountainous and difficult-to-access areas. CM Hussain said satellite connectivity was essential for monitoring glaciers and keeping track of natural disasters in the region, citing the recent natural disaster in Nepal as an example of the importance of such connectivity. He added that effective disaster response was possible only through coordination among all relevant institutions. PTA Chairman retired Gen Hafeezur Rehman told the committee that, in accordance with the directives of PM Shehbaz, the authority was taking measures to improve internet services in GB. He said obstacles and challenges affecting internet connectivity in the region would be reviewed and necessary steps would be taken to address them. The committee chairman said GB was amo­ng the most beautiful regions in the world and attracted thousands of tourists every year, but slow internet speeds remained a major issue and required immediate attention. He said no country or region could develop in the modern era without reliable internet connectivity. Therefore, Senator Hassan said, it was essential to provide the GB people with modern, high-speed and quality internet services. He said another meeting would be held in Gilgit, inviting all relevant stakeholders and private network companies to discuss improvements in internet services. Senior officials of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) briefed the committee on disaster preparedness, early warning systems, rescue facilities and available funds in GB. They also briefed the committee on the damage caused by floods, landslides, avalanches and other natural disasters during the past five years, compensation paid to victims, and relief and rescue operations. The committee chairman stressed the need to further strengthen the role of the NDMA in dealing with natural disasters in GB. He said floods and other natural disasters had caused extensive damage in various parts of the reg­ion, making it essential to ensure the timely provision of assistance to affected communities. Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) Chairman Nabeel Awan briefed the committee on the availability, transportation and storage of petroleum products and LPG in GB. He said the region had sufficient storage capacity to maintain oil reserves capable of meeting its requirements for 20 to 30 days. He also briefed the committee on oil storage facilities in Baltistan division. Senator Aamir Waliuddin Chishti directed that oil and LPG storage capacity in GB be increased. He asked Ogra officials to effectively raise issues related to oil and LPG storage in GB with the federal petroleum ministry and take necessary measures for their permanent resolution. Special Technology Zones Authority (STZA) Chairman Azfar Manzoor briefed the committee via video link on various issues concerning GB. He said the authority had previously taken steps towards establishing a special technology zone in the region and was ready to continue playing its role in this regard. The body chairman said GB was a tax-free region and, therefore, there should be no technical difficulty in establishing a special technology zone in the region.
